newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Aznar brushes aside Tietmeyer EMU worries.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Aznar brushes aside Tietmeyer EMU worries.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar brushed aside on Tuesday comments by the Bundesbank president on the wisdom of letting less stable economies -- like Spain's -- join Europe's single currency.
"It's a generic question, we're going to worry about our own (abilities)...and I think we're doing well," Aznar said at a news conference.

The conservative prime minister, whose Popular Party (PP) government has been in power for five months, has just put together a tough budget aimed at whipping Spain's economy into shape to meet the single currency criteria by next year.

Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer warned on Monday that fast track alignment of economies to meet the criteria would not create the stable, lasting environment sought in the European Monetary and Economic Union (EMU).
Aznar said Spain had made a "very clear" decision to join the single currency and credibility in the economy was growing as a result.

"We're going to continue down this road," Aznar said. "It's resulted in a notable growth of confidence in our economy. Interest rates are falling, risk premiums are falling...and Spain's road to the monetary union is clear."
Earlier, Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said future budgets and monetary decisions in Spain would aim to create stability.

"It will be a priority when it comes time to design the budget," he said, referring to Spain's committment to the EMU stability pact agreed at a meeting of European finance ministers and central bank officials in Dublin.
